coverage_notes:
SOURCES ACTUALLY USED
1) Wikipedia, 2016 Clemson Tigers football team — infobox + "Coaching staff" table (14 names). All quotes from it are HTML-page verbatim.
2) Wayback Machine capture of the official athletics site's football COACHES page: http://web.archive.org/web/20161203182304/http://www.clemsontigers.com/SportSelect.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=28500&SPID=103701&SPSID=657774 (snapshot Dec. 3, 2016 — i.e., after the ACC Championship and about five weeks before the Jan. 9, 2017 title game). Lists exactly the 10 on-field coaches with their titles. Quotes are verbatim HTML text.
3) 2016 Clemson Football Media Guide, https://issuu.com/clemsontigers/docs/2016_guide (published July 30, 2016; 212 pages). Sections used: "Football Administration" (p. 21), "Football Support Staff" (pp. 31-34) and "Strength & Conditioning" (pp. 40-41). This supplied all 42 non-on-field names.
4) Corroboration only (not cited per person): the archived 2016 Fiesta Bowl Guide PDF, http://web.archive.org/web/20170124023212/http://www.clemsontigers.com/fls/28500/pdf/football/2016-17/ClemsonBowlGuide.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=28500 — its COACHES table (p. 7) lists the same 10 on-field coaches with the same titles as of the postseason, confirming no on-field turnover between the media guide, the December site capture, and the playoff.

WHY MANY QUOTES ARE EMPTY
The media guide exists only as an Issuu publication; no PDF copy of it survives on clemsontigers.com or in the Wayback Machine (I enumerated every archived clemsontigers.com PDF for 2016-17 — only the bowl guide, a stats package, a fan guide and a parking map). Issuu's reader page contains no page text in its HTML; the text is served as a separate binary layer. I recovered the text from that layer AND visually verified every name/title against the rendered page images (reader pages 23, 33, 34, 35, 36, 42, 43) before recording it. Because none of that text can be string-matched against a fetched Issuu URL, those rows follow the instruction to set quote to "" and explain here. Every media-guide row was read off the page image, so the names and titles are exact; only the mechanical match is unavailable.

KNOWN GAPS AND CAVEATS
- Timing mismatch for support staff: the media guide is a July 2016 snapshot. I could not find any archived staff listing from December 2016/January 2017 for the non-coaching staff (the site's athletics staff-directory article, ATCLID=205504944, is archived but its body content is empty in every snapshot I tried: Sep 2016, Oct 2016, Dec 2016, Feb 2017). So for the 42 support-staff rows I can document "on staff for the 2016 season" but not independently confirm presence at the championship game. No midseason_note is set on anyone because I found no documented arrival or departure during the season.
- Zac Alley is the one name taken solely from Wikipedia; he does not appear in the media guide's Football Support Staff section, and I could not corroborate his 2016 role elsewhere. Treat that row as lower confidence.
- Deliberately excluded as athletics-department rather than football-team staff, though they appear in the same media guide: Don Munson (Director of Broadcasting, Clemson Tiger Sports Network, printed p. 34) and the Athletic Communications staff on printed p. 8 — Joe Galbraith (Assistant AD, Director), Tim Bourret (Director of Football Communications), Jonathan Gantt (Director, New & Creative Media), Sam Blackman, Brian Hennessy, Libby Kehn, Philip Sikes (Associate ACD, Secondary Football), Jeff Kallin, Nik Conklin and D.J. Gordon (Coordinator of Creative Services — a different D.J. Gordon entry from the equipment manager listed above). Tim Bourret and Philip Sikes are football-designated and could reasonably be added if the dataset counts communications staff.
- Role_category judgment calls: Cameron Aiken and Andrew Warwick carry "player development" titles and are filed as qc rather than analyst; the five S&C student administrative assistants (Estes, Goodnature, McNamara, Paruta, Wilson) are filed as sc but are students named in prose, not full-time staff, and may warrant exclusion.
- Web search was unavailable for this run (session search budget exhausted before I started), so I could not sweep contemporary news articles for additional hires, interim staff, or student/volunteer assistants beyond what the three primary sources document. Nothing in this list is inferred: every row traces to one of the sources above.
